recognize_zh: 低倍血片可見多個兩端尖細的鐮刀狀與船形紅血球，混有標靶細胞，而且許多紅血球內有圓形深紫色的 Howell-Jolly 小體；鐮刀細胞加上 Howell-Jolly 小體，指向 HbSS 合併功能性無脾。
features: Numerous irreversibly sickled cells (elongated with pointed ends) and boat-shaped cells
Many red cells contain a single small, round, dense basophilic Howell-Jolly body
Occasional larger, bluish polychromatic red cell
Variable red cell size and shape; platelets present and not clumped
Low-power (x20) view limits assessment of fine inclusions such as Pappenheimer bodies
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at low power shows marked poikilocytosis with numerous sickle cells and boat-shaped cells, together with target cells. Many red cells contain a single round, dense Howell-Jolly body, and occasional polychromatic macrocytes are present. The density of Howell-Jolly bodies indicates loss of splenic filtering function. Findings are consistent with sickle cell anemia (HbSS) with functional hyposplenism; hemoglobin separation (HPLC or electrophoresis) is required to define the genotype.

ddx.vs: HbSC shows fewer classic sickle cells and characteristic straight-edged, crystal-containing 'folded' or 'Washington monument' cells with more target cells, confirmed by HbS and HbC peaks on HPLC.
Tends to show more microcytosis and hypochromia with target cells; separation requires HbA2 quantitation, MCV, and family or DNA studies.
Surgical asplenia also produces abundant Howell-Jolly bodies and target cells but lacks sickle cells unless a sickling hemoglobin is present.
Elliptocytes have rounded, blunt ends and uniform oval shape, whereas sickle cells here are crescentic with tapered ends.
